# staark common

Shared abstract-node constructors and utilities used by the Staark renderers. Use this package when building tooling or a renderer around Staark's abstract tree; application code normally imports the same helpers from `@doars/staark`, `@doars/staark-patch`, or `@doars/staark-isomorphic`.

## Runtime and exports

Most constructors are runtime-independent. DOM conversion utilities require browser DOM APIs. The package exports its constructors and utilities from the package entry.

## Abstract nodes

```TypeScript
type NodeContent = string | MemoAbstract | NodeAbstract

node(
  type: string,
  attributesOrContents?: NodeAttributes | NodeContent[] | NodeContent,
  contents?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent,
): NodeAbstract
```

`node` only constructs an abstract object; it does not touch the DOM. The second argument can be attributes or contents. DOM renderers interpret function-valued attributes as event listeners, while the isomorphic renderer omits them. `key` is reconciliation metadata and is not emitted as an HTML or DOM attribute.

```JavaScript
node('p', 'Text')
node('button', { click: onClick }, 'Save')
```

## View helpers

```TypeScript
conditional(
  condition: any,
  onTruth: NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction,
  onFalse?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction,
): NodeContent[]

match(
  key: any,
  lookup: Record<any, NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction>,
  fallback?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction | null,
): NodeContent[]

memo(
  render: (state: any, memory: any) => NodeContent[] | NodeContent,
  memory: any,
): MemoAbstract
```

`conditional` and `match` evaluate only the selected function and normalize its result to an array. `memo` records a render function and memory value; a compatible renderer decides whether its previous subtree can be reused.

## Alternative node creation

```TypeScript
nde(selector: string, contents?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent): NodeAbstract
```

`nde` parses syntax such as `a.button#next[href=/next]`. `factory` is a proxy of tag-name functions around `node`; `fctory` combines tag-name functions with selector parsing.

```JavaScript
import { factory, fctory, nde } from '@doars/staark-common'

const { div } = factory
const { a } = fctory

div([nde('strong.notice', 'Notice')])
a('.button[href=/next]', 'Next')
```

## Utilities

- `arrayify(data)` returns `data` as an array; `arrayifyOrUndefined(data)` returns an array or `undefined`.
- `cloneRecursive(value, clones?)` deeply clones supported values while preserving cycles and shared references.
- `equalRecursive(valueA, valueB, compared?)` recursively compares supported values, including maps, sets, typed arrays, and circular structures.
- `equalPlain(valueA, valueB)` is a smaller comparison for plain data. Arrays and plain objects are compared by content and dates by time; any other object only by identity. Circular structures are never equal.
- `clonePlain(value)` copies plain data so it can later be compared with `equalPlain`, even after the original is mutated in place. Arrays and plain objects are copied recursively and dates by time; other objects and circular references are kept by reference.
- `increasingSubsequence(sources)` marks the longest increasing subsequence of a sparse number array, used to minimise DOM moves.
- `childrenToNodes(element)` converts an element's DOM children into abstract nodes using their lowercase-preserving `localName`, and requires DOM APIs. Comments become `#comment` nodes.
- `identifier(prefix)` returns a process-unique string using the prefix.
- `marker` is the abstract-node discriminator string `'n'`.
- `attributeToString(name, value)` converts an attribute value to the string written to the DOM, joining class arrays and the truthy keys of class objects.
- `suffixNameIfMultiple(attributes)` normalizes multiple select-like attribute names.
- `propertyNameToType(propertyName)` maps DOM property names to attribute types.
- `selectorToTokenizer(selector)` tokenizes the selector syntax used by `nde` and `fctory`.

## Renderer behavior

This package defines data structures, not one universal rendering policy. Attribute handling, memo support, hydration, and event binding depend on the consuming package. See `@doars/staark` for reactive DOM rendering, `@doars/staark-patch` for stateless DOM patching, and `@doars/staark-isomorphic` for HTML serialization.
